A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CausVid research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and supplementary material support reliable comparison; renamed and relocated content can be matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original video-generation benchmarks, timing measurements, human preferences, ablations, and qualitative results, including supplementary teacher comparisons.

after.justification: V3 retains original benchmark, timing, preference, and ablation results, updates the supplementary VBench-Long results, and adds a 14-minute generation example.

M1.justification: The blockwise causal transformer, ODE initialization, asymmetric distribution matching, and KV-cached inference remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 replaces per-chunk prediction and concatenation notation with an explicit masked whole-video call, clarifying the architecture already described in v1 rather than establishing a changed method.

E1.justification: Section 5.4 adds an explicitly demonstrated extreme-duration scenario through a 14-minute video, extending the tested temporal horizon beyond v1's 30-second comparisons. Training data, benchmark datasets, and the other generation and translation tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: V3 removes the bidirectional teacher from the full VBench-Long comparison in Table 7 and removes its paired qualitative comparison. The teacher remains in the main ablations, timing comparison, and preference study; other benchmark comparator memberships are unchanged.

E3.justification: The new qualitative evaluation uses a 14-minute output. Existing experiments retain the stated training budgets, resolutions, metrics, 128-prompt main evaluation, 946-prompt VBench evaluation, and user-study design. The updated leaderboard scores do not establish changes to those existing settings.

E4.justification: V3 adds an extreme-duration qualitative case in Section 5.4 and Figure 9, but removes v1 Appendix B's paired teacher comparison. The ODE-initialization and teacher-choice ablations in Table 4 and the 30-second quality analysis remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions specify seed zero for the preference-study videos and three ratings per prompt across 29 prompts, totaling 87 ratings per model pair. Neither version adds repeated-training-run information, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Table 7 substantially revises CausVid's full benchmark profile: total score changes from 82.85 to 84.27, semantic score from 79.40 to 78.75, dynamic degree from 82.20 to 92.69, and imaging quality from 70.20 to 68.88. Its leading total-score rank remains unchanged. Teacher results and paired examples are removed, and a 14-minute example is added. Tables 1–6 and preference results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 retain the same mathematical content, including the attention mask and distillation objectives. Adding a parameter subscript to the generator-distribution score function is notation; no new assumptions, derivations, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The central claims about asymmetric distillation, competitive autoregressive generation, reduced error accumulation, streaming speed, and zero-shot applications remain. V3 foregrounds its updated leading VBench-Long score in the abstract, but v1 already claimed state-of-the-art performance and the highest total score in Appendix A.

C2.justification: V3 removes v1 Appendix C's explanations of lost context beyond ten seconds and VAE-related chunk-boundary discontinuities, together with proposed remedies in Section 6. Generic long-video degradation, latency, and diversity limitations remain. The new extreme-duration example is interpreted as retaining high quality despite slight overexposure.

D1.justification: V1 promises a future code release based on an open-source model; v3 states that code and pretrained models are released. V3 also adds an official leaderboard access link. Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, and training-time disclosures remain unchanged; release contents cannot be assessed from the PDFs.

R1.justification: V3 removes four cited works: positional interpolation, YaRN, Deconvolution and Checkerboard Artifacts, and MiraData. These removals accompany shortened limitations and leaderboard discussion. The main positioning relative to autoregressive generation and diffusion distillation remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The title and some terminology change from causal generators to autoregressive diffusion models. V3 clarifies pseudocode, adds Section 5.4, and shortens the discussion and supplement by removing Appendices B and C. Most prose and the main section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds an architecture illustration and a 14-minute video montage, revises the training diagram, and removes the teacher-comparison montage. It redraws and enlarges the radar chart, removes Table 7's teacher row, and substantially rearranges supplementary displays. The main benchmark tables and existing generation galleries are largely retained.

improvement.justification: V3 improves architectural explanation, adds an extreme-duration example, and announces code/model availability. However, it removes concrete failure-mode explanations and detailed teacher comparisons. The revised Table 7 values are unexplained, and the PDFs do not establish the practical benefit of the release. These gains and losses prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
